newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sales, debt cut lift Gle des Eaux share.
newsitem.headline: Sales, debt cut lift Gle des Eaux share.

text.p: Cie Generale des Eaux shares rose on the back of positive sentiment after beating debt reduction targets for 1996, dealers and fund managers said.
Also, brokerage Dupont-Denant was highlighting the potential for the share to gain with the run up to the January 1, 1998 payment deadline on five billion francs of convertible bonds.
The stock was up 3.76 percent at 662 francs with 368,321 shares traded at 1526 GMT.

Dupont-Denant analysts Jean-Louis Lopez said that given a payment price on the bonds of 3,135 francs and the bond exchange rate of 4.4 per share, the conversion would be beneficial if the share passed 706 francs.
"Generale des Eaux will do all it can on communications and results to see that the share rises and that investors would be lured into converting their bonds," he said.
The group's debt ratio was brought back to 143 percent in 1996 and should fall to 106 percent next year, with 80 percent in sight after a bond conversion," he said.
On Friday, Generale des Eaux said it had exceeded its asset sale programme target with 13.3 billion francs of sales versus six billion in 1995 and that it had cut its debt to 48 billion francs.
It also confirmed its forecast of a 1.8 billion franc net profit for 1996.
